summary: Tacoma harbor light on Commencement Bay: post light lit 1887, wooden tower 1903, concrete tower 1933; keepers until automation in 1963.

light.note: USLHS: 38 ft above mean high water, original optic 375 mm, current optic listed as VRB 25. The record's characteristic (Fl W 5s) is not confirmed by a source read here.

structures.note: Lens lantern on a white post 12 ft above sea level (NRHP); replaced by the 1903 tower
Wooden tower with the light and fog bell; razed and burned in 1933 (NRHP)
Concrete tower, 34 ft (NRHP); USLHS records it as square without lantern; lantern and foghorn mounted on the parapet (NRHP)
Neoclassical keeper's cottage; restored by Points Northeast Historical Society (LighthouseFriends)
NRHP: original boathouse built 1903; LighthouseFriends says a boathouse was added in 1905
Frame, corrugated metal siding; moved near the boathouse (NRHP, which dates it 1903); LighthouseFriends dates a galvanized-iron oil house to 1907
Flat-roofed generator house beside the tower (NRHP)

access.note: Park open dawn to dusk; tower closed; keeper's cottage tours in season; lighthouse owned by the Coast Guard (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Lens lantern on a white post, 12 ft above sea level
Established 12 December 1887 (LighthouseFriends)
Board asks for a fog signal, estimated about $6,000
Act of 6 June 1900 appropriates $6,000 for a light and fog signal
Congress appropriates another $3,200 on 28 June 1902 (LighthouseFriends)
Wooden bell and light tower and keeper's dwelling; contract signed 5 March 1903 for $5,300
First lighting 26 October 1903
Fog bell suspended under the gable roof of the tower; clockwork striker
Storm of 29 November 1914 damaged revetments at Browns Point and New Dungeness
Illuminant changed from oil to acetylene; fixed white to flashing white
Keeper Oscar V. Brown saves three Japanese from drowning near the light station, 8 September
Light electrified; electric power installed
Wooden tower razed and burned; concrete tower built
Fog bell transferred to the College of Puget Sound; dedicated 20 February 1934
Browns Point Garden Club commemorative tablet placed on the tower, 26 May 1934
Coast Guard assumes responsibility for the light (LighthouseFriends)
Light automated; keepers withdrawn
Grounds converted to a public park
Fog bell installed at Fox Island Alliance Church
Fog bell returned to Browns Point on 25 July 2000
NRHP 89000208 (NRIS number gives the 1989 listing year; registration form prepared August 1988)
Restoration began July 2021; cost $150,000; rededication on Sunday, October 17

corrections.proposed: post light (lens lantern on a white post), built 1887; concrete tower built 1933, 10.4 m (34 ft)
corrections.why: The 1887 light was a lens lantern on a post, not a concrete tower (NRHP). The concrete tower is dated 1933 and is 34 ft (USLHS, NRHP).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NRHP form says two owners received $1,500 each; LighthouseFriends says condemnation resulted in $3,000 paid to the owner. Not resolved: the two sources name different sums and different numbers of owners.
NRHP form says the bell was cast in Philadelphia in 1852. LighthouseFriends and the Bulletin of 1934 say 1855. The 1855 date has two sources against one.
NRHP form says the clock weights were wound every 90 minutes; LighthouseFriends says every forty-five minutes. Not resolved.
Record's 11.6 m matches USLHS 38 ft above mean high water.
Record gives Fl W 5s; USLHS lists the current optic as VRB 25. No source read here gives a characteristic, so the record value is unconfirmed.

NRHP form (2) dates the boathouse and the oil house to 1903. LighthouseFriends (1) says a boathouse was added in 1905 and a galvanized-iron oil house erected in 1907. Not resolved; the story does not give these dates.
NRHP form says Philadelphia 1852; LighthouseFriends and the 1934 Bulletin say 1855. Story states both.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-22 (Haiku). Keeper roster matched by roster.py (name and position, 0.11 km); the USLHS roster lines were checked against the cached page. Browns Point story checked against NRHP form (quotes verified in the cached form), LighthouseFriends (cached), the 1895, 1901 Light-House Board reports (scan p. 406 and p. 265, both confirmed by corpus.py page), and the Lighthouse Service Bulletins (PDF pages 2, 12, 17, 52 and 8 confirmed by corpus.py page; the 1931 quotation is OCR and was read from the page). The 1934 Bulletin tablet inscription is garbled in OCR, so the story cites LighthouseFriends for the tablet and its inscription. The 1931 fog account is an OCR-interleaved text; the quoted phrases were taken from clean lines. 'Three Japanese' is the Bulletin's own wording for the 1917 rescue (OCR 'rescueu'), kept as a quotation-level paraphrase. Robert V. Deason (roster) vs Robert B. Deason (LighthouseFriends); the roster spelling is used. Living-people rule: post-1960 USCG roster names (Shoultz, Hazard, Roberts, Amundsen) are in the JSON only as the roster prints them and are not named in the prose. Current status (2026) not verified: the Parks Tacoma and Points Northeast Historical Society pages returned 403 to fetch_text, so the 'Today' section rests on LighthouseFriends (2021 restoration, tour schedule from an older page). Check hours before publishing. LSB 1937 list gives Oscar V. Brown '47 years' (OCR, interleaved); conflicts with 36 years, so it is not used. The Smith Island, Cape Flattery and New Dungeness service of Brown is from LighthouseFriends only. Newspapers cited by the NRHP form (Tacoma Daily Ledger 1900 and 1933; Heilman 1930) were not read; the newspaper search was not run for this station.
